Lesson 5 · Guided route

Uncertainty and conditional comparisons: guided case

Do powered fixtures improve calibration output across service ages?

Work through 5 selected steps. The short case gives the decision first; the technical appendix holds the complete model and derivations.

Short caseTechnical appendix
Guided steps
  1. 01. Introduce Cedar without inheriting the previous model
  2. 02. Read an adjusted coefficient as a conditional comparison
  3. 03. Hold the sample fixed when models change
  4. 04. Let the fixture comparison vary with age
  5. 05. Deliver a conditional, testable claim

Guided step 01 / 5

Introduce Cedar without inheriting the previous model

Cedar contains 260 simulated calibration rigs. Y is throughput in units/hour; E is service age in years; D marks a powered fixture; A is a tool setting between zero and one; bench category is amber, blue or copper. The generator uses seed 550829 and all features are available before calibration.

E ∼ Uniform(0,12); P(D=1|E) = logistic(−1+0.2E); Ec = E−6.
Y = 70 + 2Ec − 0.08Ec² + 5D + 1.1D Ec + 4A + 0.7EcA + bench offset + (3+0.4E)Z.

A is independent Uniform(0,1), Z is independent standard normal, and bench probabilities are 0.40, 0.35 and 0.25 with offsets 0, 4 and −3. Older rigs are more likely to have powered fixtures. This association makes the unconditional fixture contrast different from a comparison at a common service age.

Pause and explain

Why explicitly change the data passport between examples?

Compare your reasoning
Units, sampling, error structure and estimands changed. Carrying a previous case’s assumptions forward without restating them would make the inference misleading.

Guided step 02 / 5

Read an adjusted coefficient as a conditional comparison

Additive approximation: Ŷ = b₀ + bD D + bE(E−6).

In the same-row additive model, the fixture coefficient is 2.489 units/hour. It compares the two fitted fixture groups at a common service age while imposing parallel service-age slopes. The unadjusted difference is 10.449. Adding a variable changes the comparison being made; it does not automatically reveal a “true effect.”

Unadjusted group means — chart data
GroupThroughput units/hour
No fixture68.8388
Powered fixture79.2877

The known generator has fixture-by-age interaction and curvature, so this additive fit is deliberately incomplete. Its coefficient is a linear projection coefficient, not the constant conditional fixture contrast of the full generator.

Pause and explain

What does “holding service age constant” mean algebraically?

Compare your reasoning
Compare two fitted values with the same service-age input and different D. It does not mean the data physically held each rig fixed or randomly assigned its fixture.

Guided step 03 / 5

Hold the sample fixed when models change

Every Cedar coefficient comparison uses the same 260 rows. That is crucial: a coefficient can move because controls changed, because rows changed, or both. If a newly added covariate has missing values, first refit the shorter model on the common complete-case sample before attributing the difference to adjustment.

Composition differs across fixture groups
Fixture groupMean service yearsMean throughput
No fixture4.37268.839
Powered fixture6.90479.288

A complete-case sample can itself be selected. A defensible workflow records eligibility, missingness, measurement units and duplicate handling before interpreting adjusted coefficients. Here no outcome-based filtering or missing-data deletion occurs.

Pause and explain

Can the exact omitted-variable identity survive using different rows in the short and long models?

Compare your reasoning
Not in its usual same-sample form. Its algebra assumes identical outcomes, rows and weights, plus the stated nested regressors.

Guided step 04 / 5

Let the fixture comparison vary with age

Fixture contrast at age E = bD + bD×E(E−6).

Centering age at six makes the main fixture coefficient answer a meaningful reference-point question. The interaction coefficient says how the fixture contrast changes per additional service year. Neither coefficient alone describes the contrast at every age. HC3 uncertainty for each contrast uses the full covariance, including the covariance between main and interaction terms.

Pause and explain

What happens to fitted values if age is centered somewhere else?

Compare your reasoning
They remain the same when all lower-order and interaction terms are transformed consistently. Main-effect coefficients change their reference point, not the underlying fitted surface.

Guided step 05 / 5

Deliver a conditional, testable claim

A careful Cedar handoff separates four statements: the unadjusted fixture difference is 10.449 units/hour; the additive age-adjusted coefficient is 2.489; the full model permits age-varying contrasts; and robust uncertainty addresses heteroskedasticity under independent sampling. The exact additive coefficient change is verified by the auxiliary regression, not explained causally by algebra alone.

  • For a coefficient: name the contrast, reference point and covariance method.
  • For an average: use uncertainty in the conditional mean.
  • For a new outcome: add the appropriate conditional outcome variation.
  • For action: investigate design, measurement and consequences beyond the fitted residual.

The notebook reproduces all estimates, interval endpoints, covariance calculations, tests and residual rankings. Its assertions verify FWL, the omitted-variable identity and reference-category invariance. Next, Lesson 6 turns the emphasis from explaining a fitted sample to forecasting genuinely new cases.

Pause and explain

What is the strongest unsupported leap to avoid?

Compare your reasoning
Do not turn an adjusted association or a residual into a causal conclusion or an individual operational judgment without the additional evidence that decision requires.

Compare with the known truth

Reveal the generator truth

In the generator, the fixture difference is 5 units per hour at six years of service and changes by 1.1 units for each additional year. One fitted coefficient need not equal that whole effect function.

This comparison is possible because the case is synthetic. The full generating process is in the appendix.
